overview: This Senate resolution marks one year since the June 1, 2025, attack on people taking part in a peaceful walk in Boulder, Colorado, organized by Run for Their Lives in support of hostages taken in the October 7, 2023, Hamas attack on Israel. It describes the attack as an act of antisemitic terrorism, honors Karen Diamond, an 82-year-old participant who died of her injuries, and offers condolences to survivors and their families. It commends the local Jewish community, first responders, medical staff and prosecutors for their response. It also reaffirms the Senate's commitment to fighting antisemitism and hate-motivated violence and affirms Jewish Americans' right to gather and live openly without fear. It does not change any law or spending. As of June 22, 2026, the Senate had approved it.
for: Supporters say it honors the victims, recognizes the community's response, and sends a clear message against antisemitic violence.
against: Critics say it is symbolic and does not change any law or add resources to prevent hate crimes.
